item.title: PLA Navy Marine Corps' Amphibious Elite Challenge Tournament Concludes
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-24
BEIJING, Sept. 24 -- The second stage of the "Versatility Cup" Amphibious Elite Challenge Tournament, held by the Marine Corps of the Chinese PLA Navy, concluded in an area of southern Fujian Province on September 23, 2026. The second stage lasted three days, with more than 1,000 Marines competing in multiple events across major combat-oriented categories such as "Armored Assault"and "Sharpshooter." The "Armored Assault"event was divided into three sub-events: "Amphibious Assault,""Ironclad Assault"and "Mengshi Assault,"comprehensively testing the troops' overall combat capabilities in squad-level battlefield maneuver and coordinated assault. The events ranged from squad coordination to individual limits, and from maritime obstacle crossing to precision sniping, directly linking the competition ground to the real battlefield. Competitors had to complete various tasks under combined conditions of physical exertion, psychological pressure, and environmental interference. The tournament tested the participants' training standards under complex battlefield conditions, further honing the troops' combat capabilities. (Video Editor: Yang Xueqing)

item.title: Xi kicks off highly-anticipated U.S. visit in grand welcome
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-24
Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan step out of the airplane cabin upon their arrival at Joint Base Andrews in the United States on Sept. 23, 2026. (Xinhua/Liu Bin) * China and the United States should work in the same direction and promote a stable relationship featuring cooperation as the mainstay, moderate competition, manageable differences and promises of peace, Xi said in a written speech upon his arrival. * Xi said he looks forward to having in-depth exchanges with Trump on major issues concerning bilateral relations and the world situation, constantly enriching the constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability, and expanding the space for exchanges and cooperation in various fields between the two countries. WASHINGTON, Sept. 24 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived at Joint Base Andrews on Wednesday afternoon for a state visit to the United States at the invitation of U.S. President Donald Trump. The visit has drawn wide attention as the two countries seek to stabilize their relationship, deepen cooperation and work together to address global challenges. RARE PLANESIDE WELCOME Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, received a rare planeside greeting by Trump and his wife, Melania Trump, upon their arrival. After Xi and Peng descended from their plane, the two presidential couples shook hands and exchanged greetings on the tarmac. A red carpet was rolled out for the Chinese presidential couple, with honor guards lining up on both sides to pay their respects. Two American children presented bouquets of flowers to Xi and Peng. The welcome ceremony also included a 21-gun salute, the playing of the national anthems of both countries and a military flyover. A gun salute is fired to welcome Chinese President Xi Jinping upon his arrival at Joint Base Andrews for a state visit to the United States at the invitation of U.S. President Donald Trump, Sept. 23, 2026. (Xinhua/Yao Dawei) The 21-gun salute is among the highest military honors accorded to a visiting head of state, but is rarely rendered at an airport. The gesture is notable even by broader diplomatic standards, as the arrangement has been described by U.S. media as a "rare" and "unusual" departure from protocol, as U.S. presidents typically receive visiting foreign leaders at the White House rather than greet them at the airport. Xi's arrival kicked off a three-day state visit to the United States, which comes just months after Trump's China trip in May. The exchange of visits between the two heads of state within six months is of historic and milestone significance, a Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson said on Monday. PARTNERS, NOT RIVALS In a written speech upon his arrival, Xi extended sincere greetings and best wishes to the U.S. people on behalf of the Chinese people. China and the United States are both great countries, and the two peoples are both great peoples, Xi said, adding that the two peoples have maintained friendly exchanges for a long time and their interests are deeply intertwined. Chinese President Xi Jinping arrives at Joint Base Andrews on Sept. 23, 2026, for a state visit to the United States at the invitation of U.S. President Donald Trump. (Xinhua/Li Xiang) China and the United States should be partners, not rivals, he said, noting that the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and making America great again can go hand in hand, and that the two countries can help each other succeed and advance the well-being of the whole world. Xi noted that he and Trump agreed to build a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability during Trump's visit to China in May, which has provided strategic guidance for the future development of bilateral ties. China and the United States should work in the same direction and promote a stable relationship featuring cooperation as the mainstay, moderate competition, manageable differences and promises of peace, Xi said. He said China and the United States, as two major countries, should find a right way to get along in the new era. Xi emphasized that the world is developing and times are changing, but the historical logic of peaceful coexistence between China and the United States has not changed, the goodwill of friendly exchanges between the two peoples has not changed, and the general expectations of the international community for China and the United States have not changed. Xi said he looks forward to having in-depth exchanges with Trump on major issues concerning bilateral relations and the world situation, constantly enriching the constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability, and expanding the space for exchanges and cooperation in various fields between the two countries. With joint efforts, Xi said he believes the visit is sure to be fruitful, and will enhance the well-being of the two peoples and add hope for world peace. U.S. children present flowers to Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan at Joint Base Andrews in the United States, Sept. 23, 2026. (Xinhua/Zhai Jianlan) WIDE EXPECTATIONS It is a very important visit, coming at a very important time and against the backdrop of a particularly difficult global political landscape, said Roland Henwood, a lecturer and political commentator at the Department of Political Sciences at the University of Pretoria. The significance of the visit extends well beyond bilateral ties, as what happens between China and the United States affects the whole world, said Henwood. Noting that the two leaders have a good relationship and hold regular contacts and good communication, he said that it is vital to have sustained engagement at the presidential level to provide strategic direction and stability for the bilateral ties. Erastus Mwencha, former deputy chairperson of the African Union Commission, said the state visit sends an important signal -- diplomacy remains available as an instrument for managing differences and preventing miscalculation. It should also be read as part of a sequence rather than an isolated event -- the Busan meeting, Trump's state visit to China in May, and now this reciprocal visit -- each building the kind of sustained contact that a single meeting cannot provide, said Mwencha. Beyond high-level diplomacy, experts pointed to several areas where continued China-U.S. cooperation could have broader international implications. Chinese President Xi Jinping is welcomed upon his arrival in the United States on Sept. 23, 2026. (Xinhua/Lu Ye) Artificial intelligence (AI) is one such area. China and the United States have the technological capabilities and international influence to play an important role in addressing the potential risks posed by AI, said Pascal Sery, a financial expert and former member of the National Assembly of Cote d'Ivoire. They can strengthen dialogue and cooperation on AI safety, governance, ethics and international rules, and work toward broader international consensus, he said. Abu Bakr al-Deeb, an advisor at the Cairo-based Arab Center for Research and Studies, said counternarcotics is one of the areas where cooperation between China and the United States can produce very practical results. Drug trafficking and other forms of transnational crime do not stop at national borders, so countries have a common interest in sharing information and coordinating their efforts, he said. There have already been concrete examples of cooperation this year as Chinese and U.S. authorities have worked together on drug-related cases, including cases involving trafficking and new psychoactive substances, he added. Experts also pointed to the broader role the two countries can play in addressing global challenges. Cavince Adhere, a Kenya-based international relations scholar, said the two countries, as the world's two largest economies, have a responsibility to reduce friction and help safeguard the stability of the global economy and supply chains. Achieving stability of their relationship is "a public good," he said. "Reduced U.S.-China friction lowers the risk of global supply chain fragmentation."

item.title: Japan Should Stop Sowing Discord in the South China Sea: Defense Spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-24
BEIJING, Sept. 24 -- "We urge the Japanese side to offer a clear explanation of its accelerating 'remilitarization' efforts, and stop sowing discord and undermining peace and stability in the South China Sea," said Senior Colonel Jiang Bin, spokesperson for China's Ministry of National Defense, at a press conference on Thursday. In the wake of the incident provoked by a Philippine government vessel near Xianbin Jiao of China's Nansha Qundao, the Japanese Embassy in the Philippines quickly posted on social media that it's "gravely concerned" over the "dangerous actions" by China, and portrayed itself as "upholding the rule of law and opposing any actions which increase tensions". In response, the spokesperson pointed out that it's clear and evident that the Philippine government vessel made provocations near Xianbin Jiao and deliberately rammed a China Coast Guard vessel. Though Japan is not a country directly involved in the South China Sea issue, it has actively joined the Philippine side in distorting facts.The real intention is to make waves in the South China Sea and fish in muddy waters. The spokesperson then emphasized that the Chinese side firmly opposes this behavior. He added that the Japanese side has been strengthening its collusion with the Philippines by providing weapons and sending troops to the Philippines for joint exercises, during which it launched offensive missiles overseas for the first time. "The Japanese side is attempting to break away from the post-war international order and revive its old dream of military expansion. This is a real threat to regional peace and stability," stressed the spokesperson.

China and the United States are both great countries, and the two peoples are both great peoples, Xi said in the speech, adding that the two peoples have maintained friendly exchanges for a long time and their interests are deeply intertwined. China and the United States should be partners, not rivals, he said, noting that the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and making America great again can go hand in hand, and that the two countries can help each other succeed and advance the well-being of the whole world. Xi noted that he and Trump agreed to build a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability during Trump's visit to China in May, which has provided strategic guidance for the future development of bilateral ties. China and the United States should work in the same direction, promote a stable relationship featuring cooperation as the mainstay, moderate competition, manageable differences, and promises of peace, Xi said. He said China and the United States, as two major countries, should find a right way to get along in the new era. Xi emphasized that the world is developing and times are changing, but the historical logic of peaceful coexistence between China and the United States has not changed, the goodwill of friendly exchanges between the two peoples has not changed, and the general expectations of the international community for China and the United States have not changed. Xi said he looks forward to having in-depth exchanges with Trump on major issues concerning bilateral relations and the world situation, constantly enriching the connotation of the constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability, and expanding the space for exchanges and cooperation in various fields between the two countries. Xi said he also looks forward to engaging extensively with people from all walks of life in the United States to deepen friendship. With joint efforts, Xi said he believes the visit is sure to be fruitful, and will enhance the well-being of the two peoples and add hope for world peace. item.title: China-Laos "Peace Train-2026" Medical Service Mission Concludes
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-23
By Zhou Na, Liu Xiaowei, Yang Chao, Tan Yuzhou and Wang Yong BEIJING, Sept. 23 -- On September 21, the Chinese medical team participating in the China-Laos "Peace Train-2026" medical service mission successfully completed its seven-day mission at four locations in Laos, namely Vientiane, Pakse, Savannakhet and Attapeu, providing medical services during a total of 6,275 patient visits. The "Peace Train" medical team selected more than 70 key medical experts and formed four specialized medical detachments covering 31 specialties, including cardiovascular medicine, orthopedics, emergency medicine, respiratory medicine, ophthalmology and traditional Chinese medicine. The team provided free medical consultations, health checkups, multidisciplinary consultations, medical science education and other services benefiting the local residents. On the evening of September 22, the Chinese medical team boarded a medical train and departed from Vientiane Station via the China-Laos Railway on its journey home, marking the successful conclusion of the 17-day China-Laos "Peace Train-2026" joint humanitarian medical rescue exercise and medical service mission. (Video Editor: Cheng Sihao)

item.title: China urges Japan to draw lessons from history, win trust through concrete actions: spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-23
BEIJING, Sept. 23 (Xinhua) -- China on Wednesday urged Japan to draw lessons from history, deeply reflect on the past, and win the trust of its Asian neighbors and the international community through concrete actions. Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun made the remarks at a regular press briefing when asked to comment on Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's speech at the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday, in which she said that Japan is a peace-loving country and called for the deletion of the "enemy state clauses" from the UN Charter. "Compared with what Japan says, the international community is more concerned about what Japan does," Guo said. He said post-war Japan's concept of being a "peace-loving country" was built on deeply reflecting on its history and making a complete break with militarism. "In fact, the current Japanese administration not only denies its history of aggression and whitewashes its war crimes, but also continues to build up its military and expand its armaments, accelerates 'remilitarization,' seeks to abandon the Three Non-Nuclear Principles and revise the pacifist Constitution, and openly challenges the post-war international order," Guo said. Japan has become a prominent factor threatening regional peace and stability, he stressed. This year marks the 81st anniversary of the founding of the United Nations and the 80th anniversary of the opening of the Tokyo Trial, Guo said, adding that Japan joined the UN on the premise of acknowledging the crimes of militarism and accepting the UN Charter in its entirety. The "enemy state clauses" in the UN Charter constitute important institutional arrangements aimed at preventing fascism and militarism from once again threatening international peace and security, and provide important institutional safeguards for upholding the post-war international order, Guo said. "To this day, they still carry important practical significance," he said. "We urge the Japanese side to draw lessons from history, deeply reflect on the past, and win the trust of its Asian neighbors and the international community through concrete actions," Guo said.
